## Authentication

Credentials depend on which `STACSource` you use, and only one is needed:

- **`MPCSource`** (Microsoft Planetary Computer) works with no credentials
  at all -- search and asset access both fall back to anonymous requests.
  A subscription key is optional and only raises the request rate limit,
  useful for large batch runs. Get one free at
  [planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/account](https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/account),
  then set it as an environment variable:
  ```bash
  export MPC_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY=your-key-here
  ```
  It's picked up automatically; nothing needs to be passed in code or in
  a config file. Never commit the key value itself anywhere in the repo.
- **`OPERASource`** (NASA OPERA RTC-S1 via ASF/CMR) requires a NASA
  Earthdata Login. Create a free account at
  [urs.earthdata.nasa.gov](https://urs.earthdata.nasa.gov), then follow
  NASA's own `.netrc` setup instructions:
  [urs.earthdata.nasa.gov/documentation/for_users/data_access/curl_and_wget](https://urs.earthdata.nasa.gov/documentation/for_users/data_access/curl_and_wget).
  In short, add an entry to `~/.netrc`:
  ```
  machine urs.earthdata.nasa.gov
    login your-username
    password your-password
  ```
  and restrict its permissions so other users on the machine can't read
  your credentials:
  ```bash
  chmod 600 ~/.netrc
  ```
  `requests` picks this up automatically on the OAuth redirect; no
  environment variable or code change needed.

## Grid generation

Both ways of running AutoFloods (see [Running
AutoFloods](#running-autofloods) below) need a tiling grid
(`grid_shapefile`) -- a shapefile/geopackage of AOI tile polygons with
`ID`, `zone`, and `dry_month` columns. If you don't already have one,
`autofloods.grid.generate_grid` builds one from an AOI boundary, or
`flood_mapper` can generate it for you on the fly by passing `aoi=`
instead of `grid_shapefile=` (see [Examples](examples.qmd)).

Two modes:

- **`mode='mgrs'`** (default) -- tiles aligned to MGRS 100km grid
  squares, one fishnet per UTM zone/latitude band the AOI intersects.
  Recommended with `OPERASource`, since OPERA RTC-S1 is natively
  MGRS-tiled -- MGRS-aligned tiles avoid extra clipping/reprojection
  against the source data's own grid. This is a geometric
  approximation of true MGRS tiling (a 100km-aligned fishnet computed
  per UTM zone, labeled via the `mgrs` package), not NASA's
  authoritative MGRS tile database -- interior tiles match exactly,
  but tiles right at a UTM zone boundary may not match OPERA's own
  irregular boundary tiles.
- **`mode='utm_fishnet'`** -- a fixed-size fishnet (`tile_size_km` per
  side, default 100) in the AOI's UTM zone(s), independent of MGRS.

```python
from autofloods.grid import generate_grid
from shapely.geometry import box

aoi = box(85.0, 25.0, 85.5, 25.5)  # or a shapefile/geopackage path, or a GeoDataFrame

# MGRS mode
mgrs_grid = generate_grid(aoi, mode='mgrs', dry_months='04,05',
                           output_path='resources/my_mgrs_grid.gpkg')

# UTM fishnet mode, 50km tiles
fishnet_grid = generate_grid(aoi, mode='utm_fishnet', tile_size_km=50,
                              dry_months='04,05',
                              output_path='resources/my_fishnet_grid.gpkg')
```

`dry_months` (e.g. `"04,05"`) is required to actually run the pipeline
with the generated grid -- dry season is climate knowledge, not
derivable from AOI geometry. Only the Northern Hemisphere is currently
supported (see `generate_grid`'s docstring in the [API
reference](reference/index.qmd)).

## Running AutoFloods

There are two ways to run AutoFloods: the `flood_mapper` class directly
in a notebook/script (more control), or a config file + the runner
script (fastest way to launch a real job, no code to write). Both use
the same underlying pipeline and produce the same output. See
[Examples](examples.qmd) for full walkthroughs of both.
